text: Ravi's payment just failed. Priya, the organizer, didn't chase him. Here's what her treasurer did next.
Her rules, in Hindi, go in. Turnkeeper compiles them into a frozen charter: pot order, fees, quorum, hash.
Each member sees the fees up front, then approves the schedule once, on PayPal.
Three days out, the forecast flags Ravi: late twice, and paid three weeks early. He gets a nudge in Hindi.
Salary comes Friday. That becomes a promise with a date.
The members' agents answer inside their mandates. Ravi's asks him first. Four yeses are needed, and Priya taps once.
The agent reschedules the board, and sends Ravi an invoice with a QR code.
The ledger checks out, and PayPal Payouts sends Dev the pot, net of fees, with PayPal's own IDs.
A two hundred thirty dollar charge, over Ravi's mandate, is refused before PayPal is called.
Round four is clean: six charges, one payout, and Priya typed nothing.
And the full story ran live on the PayPal sandbox.
